- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp price spikes.
- Underestimates when true outcomes show strong mean reversion or sudden drops following high peaks.
- Over-anticipates volatility; forecasts tend to overshoot after recent spikes, then correct downward.
- Forecasts lag behind true outcomes in the first 5–7 days, especially when true values are volatile or downward trending.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices in the middle of the forecast horizon, particularly when historical mean is elevated.
- When true outcomes show a clear upward trend, model often fails to capture the full magnitude of the rise, especially in the final 5–10 days.
- Model underestimates when true outcomes are clustered at the high end of the range (e.g., >36), especially if preceded by a spike.
- Forecasts are overly smooth; fail to capture abrupt reversals or sudden drops in the last 5–7 days of the horizon.
